analysis: The PR changes docs/provider/cli-reference.md only. The sole patch hunk (head line ~1732) adds a table row mapping the env vars DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS to EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (prefillChunkKey, stepTokenBudgetKey). That hunk sits in the environment-forwarding table. It is outside the two supplied head_text units, which cover lines 1-834, so the new row was not directly visible. The surrounding text I could examine is documentation only: GLM qualification, cache, logout/revocation, switch and autopilot descriptions. I found no code, credential handling, authorization, attestation or encryption behavior changed in the supplied evidence. The documented behavior is consistent with T-041 (SSD prefix cache, 30-minute TTL, kill switch) and with A-008/T-053 (logout revokes the token itself over HTTPS with no redirects; HTTP 204 is the only confirmed revocation). The PR makes no claim that weakens these. Unverified: the new row implies these variables are forwarded into the launchd daemon environment. That could let a local operator tune prefill chunk and step token budgets, which are availability and performance knobs. The Swift forwarding code is not supplied, so no security conclusion can be drawn. The operator is already the adversary in TB-003 and the variables carry no secrets. The row is likely benign, but the actual forwarding and validation bounds in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift and LaunchAgent.swift were not reviewed. No findings.
